item.research_question: How does the addition of Cr to the HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy affect its phase composition, microstructure, and room-temperature mechanical properties, specifically regarding the synergy between strength and ductility?
item.material_system: HfMoTaTiZr (30.0 at% Hf, 16.1 at% Mo, 30.4 at% Ta, 8.1 at% Ti, 15.4 at% Zr) and HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 (28.8 at% Hf, 15.5 at% Mo, 29.1 at% Ta, 7.7 at% Ti, 14.7 at% Zr, 4.2 at% Cr)
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting in an inert gas atmosphere; ingots re-melted at least 5 times to improve chemical homogeneity; weight loss did not exceed 0.5 wt%
item.test_conditions: Room temperature; Vickers hardness with 0.3 kg load and 15 s dwelling time; compression tests on cylindrical samples (3 mm diameter, 6 mm height) at a ram speed of 0.008 mm s−1 (strain rate 0.001/s)
key_findings: The addition of 4.2 at% Cr led to the formation of a Laves phase in addition to the BCC phase, whereas the base alloy was single-phase BCC.
The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 reached 535.8 Hv0.3, which is 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr (460.1 Hv0.3).
The yield strength of HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 reached 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa, which is 207.5 MPa higher than HfMoTaTiZr (1543.1 ± 40.9 MPa).
The fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 reached 14.0 ± 2.9%, which is 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr (11.6 ± 4.0%).
The volume fraction of the Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 was estimated to be 3.8%.
The lattice parameter of the BCC phase decreased from 3.392 Å in HfMoTaTiZr to 3.325 Å in HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 due to Cr dissolution.
HfMoTaTiZr exhibited intergranular and cleavage fracture modes, while HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 showed quasi-cleavage fracture in BCC grains and ductile dimple fracture in the Laves phase.
item.mechanism: The enhancement in strength is attributed to solid solution hardening caused by Cr dissolution in the BCC phase (due to lattice distortion) and the presence of the hard intermetallic Laves phase. The improvement in ductility is attributed to the formation of a continuous reticulated structure of the Laves phase, which hinders crack propagation and compensates for the plasticity loss typically caused by brittle intermetallics.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that the Laves phase is a complex multicomponent intermetallic phase temporarily denoted as Cr2(Ti, Zr, Hf, Ta) because its diffraction peaks do not match standard binary patterns.
quotes: 4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase.
The yield strength and fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr.

Solid solution hardening and the presence of the intermetallic Laves phase are believed to be responsible for the enhancement in strength and the formation of a reticulated structure of the Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 results in the improvement in ductility.
